svg.aria-label: Why a 203 dpi driver shrinks a label designed at 300 dpi
svg.title: Why a 203 dpi driver shrinks a label designed at 300 dpi

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Why a 203 dpi driver shrinks a label designed at 300 dpi

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: The driver turns the format into a fixed number of dots at its own resolution; the printhead then prints those dots at its real density, so a dpi mismatch scales every label.

text.font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'Segoe UI Web', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fix lives on the print server: swap the queue's driver (Set-Printer -DriverName), keep the port and queue name, then ruler test and LIMS reprint. Controls: CM-2, CM-3, CM-6.

svg.text: Generalised design: no client names, tenant IDs, addresses or data. Icons are simplified originals, not Microsoft artwork.
